_doc: Approval-gate rules for implementing-cdk-from-spec (core/gate/spec-approval-gate.py, plugin mode). Each setting carries a why; each command rule carries examples that the gate's unit tests check. Rule ids start with cdk- because plugin mode merges every skill's rules and the gate's tests require unique, stack-prefixed ids. A rule whose decision is write decides nothing itself: its writes object names what the matched command writes as a side effect (paths relative to the directory it works in, directory_options, file_options, path_options, operands), and the gate judges that like any other write, so it is denied inside the project before approval.
writable_why: Before approval only the plan, its ledger and planning notes may change. .claude/ holds tooling, not product.
approval_why: The skill asks the user to reply 'approve'. Looser words such as 'ok' or 'go' also answer unrelated questions and would unlock edits by accident.

command_rules.why: cdk diff --method auto (the default) and --method change-set create a CloudFormation change set with the deploy role (ref-cli-cmd-diff.html). It is the skill's replacement evidence, and it reaches a live account, so the user confirms each run. --method template uses the lookup role and creates nothing.
command_rules.message: this cdk diff creates a CloudFormation change set in the target account with the deploy role. Approve if this is the change-set diff the plan names, against the account you expect.

command_rules.why: These change an account: deploy and watch deploy stacks, destroy deletes them, bootstrap deploys the CDKToolkit stack, import adopts existing resources, orphan detaches resources from a stack, publish-assets uploads assets (ref-cli-cmd.html). The skill stops at a validated app and the change-set diff; the operator deploys.
command_rules.message: this changes stacks or resources in an AWS account. The skill never deploys; approve only if you asked for this exact command.

command_rules.why: cdk refactor calls CloudFormation's refactoring API and, in a non-interactive environment, proceeds without prompting (ref-cli-cmd-refactor.html). Only --dry-run, which prints the mapping without applying it, is planning evidence.
command_rules.message: this cdk refactor changes logical IDs in a deployed stack and does not prompt when run non-interactively. Approve only if the user asked for the refactor itself; the skill's evidence is cdk refactor --dry-run.

command_rules.why: The CloudFormation best-practices page says cdk validate runs CloudFormation pre-deployment validation, which is a service-side check of an account; the CDK CLI command reference read on 2026-10-16 does not list the command. The offline equivalent, the CloudFormationValidatePlugin, already runs in cdk synth.
command_rules.message: cdk validate runs CloudFormation's service-side pre-deployment validation against an account. Approve only if you want that account-level check now.

command_rules.why: Planning and verification are read-only. A mutating AWS call from the model bypasses the CDK app and the pipeline, and drifts the stacks.
command_rules.message: this AWS CLI call can change live resources outside the CDK app. Approve only if you intend it.

command_rules.why: A new dependency (cdk-nag, a construct library, a test tool) is a design decision the approved plan names with its version. A package that fails to install may be a hallucinated or squatted name, so it never gets a silent substitute.
command_rules.message: this installs or adds a Python package. Approve only if the approved plan names it (and this exact version), or you want it anyway.

command_rules.why: The CDK CLI and any Node-based validation plugin are installed by the user's choice: a missing tool is reported, never installed silently, and a failed install never gets a substitute package.
command_rules.message: this installs Node packages. Approve only if you want this exact package installed.

command_rules.why: In a Java CDK app dependencies live in pom.xml, and Maven installs them on the next build (work-with-cdk-java.html); a pom.xml edit is a gated write. These goals fetch or rewrite dependencies outside that path, so the user confirms them.
command_rules.message: this fetches or rewrites Maven dependencies outside pom.xml review. Approve only if the approved plan names the change.

command_rules.why: Validation tools (cfn-lint, cfn-guard, the CDK CLI) are installed by the user's choice; a missing tool is reported, not installed silently.
command_rules.message: this installs software. Approve only if you want this exact package installed.

command_rules.why: Commands that synthesise the app write the cloud assembly to cdk.out (ref-cli-cmd-synth.html), and when a lookup's context value is missing the CLI "stores the resulting context information in the cdk.context.json file" (context.html); cdk context --reset or --clear and acknowledge rewrite that file, and the app command itself runs in the project (target/ for a Java app, __pycache__/ for Python). Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this cdk command synthesises the app where it runs, writing cdk.out/ and possibly cdk.context.json and the app's build output. Before approval synthesise a copy outside the project: mkdir -p "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<slug>-synth" && tar -C . --exclude ./cdk.out --exclude ./.git -cf - . | tar -C "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<slug>-synth" -xf -, then, in a separate Bash call, run cdk synth --quiet in that directory. Write the path with ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}: an unset $TMPDIR or a $(mktemp -d) result is a target the gate cannot resolve, and it is denied.

command_rules.why: npm install installs into node_modules and updates package-lock.json (npm install); --prefix (-C) "forces non-global commands to run in the specified folder" (npm config), and pnpm -C/--dir runs "as if pnpm was started in <path>" (pnpm CLI). -g installs into the global prefix instead. Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this installs Node packages into node_modules/ in the project. Planning installs nothing: report a missing package, name it in the plan, and install after approval.

command_rules.why: Maven's lifecycle phases and the build plugins' goals write the build output into target/ ("The target directory is used to house all output of the build", Maven standard directory layout), in the project of the pom -f names or the working directory. Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in. After approval the build is routine verification and the write is allowed.
command_rules.message: this Maven build writes target/ in the project. Planning is read-only: read pom.xml and the sources instead of building, and build after the plan is approved.

command_rules.why: python -m venv DIR "creates the target directory" with the environment in it (Python venv documentation). Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in.
command_rules.message: this creates a virtual environment in the directory it names. Never refresh the project's environment before approval; a missing or broken environment is reported with the setup command from the project's rules.

command_rules.why: Inside a virtual environment pip "will install Python packages into a virtual environment without needing to be told to do so" (Python venv documentation): the environment VIRTUAL_ENV names, or the one whose bin/ holds the pip or python run (.venv/bin/pip, .venv/bin/python -m pip). A virtual environment inside the project is part of it. Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in. Outside a virtual environment (and with --user, --target, --prefix or --root, which the gate models separately) the install lands outside the project and only the dependency rule asks.
command_rules.message: this pip call installs into or removes from a virtual environment inside the project. Planning installs nothing: name the dependency in the plan, and install it after approval.
